title: OmniVia Core Application Contract v1 - governed analysis payloads
description: Request and result payloads for the governed analysis operation `analysis.start`. The payload carries a governed reference to an exact metric or Data View revision, a bounded temporal scope, the requested use class, exact typed parameters as JSON data, explicit output bounds and a purpose reference. It carries no SQL, no connection string, no filesystem path, no function name and no executable fragment of any kind: the server resolves policy, source handles and physical execution. Authentication, correlation, idempotency and purpose authority remain in the request envelope and are deliberately not duplicated here. Milestone 1 of the structured-data programme defines decoding and refusal only: every well-formed request is answered with the typed outcome `dependency_unavailable`, and the result type below is reserved and never returned by the milestone-1 build.

AnalysisUseClass.title: AnalysisUseClass
AnalysisUseClass.description: The requested result-use class. `action_input` is deliberately absent from the v1 vocabulary: action consumption is denied until an accepted action-input policy exists (UDL-D06), and a request naming it is refused as `invalid_request` rather than decoded as an admitted use class.

BusinessDate.title: BusinessDate
BusinessDate.description: A calendar date in the business timezone, without a time or offset. Distinct from a UTC instant: the envelope records instants; this type records a business-date boundary.

BusinessTimezone.title: BusinessTimezone
BusinessTimezone.description: An IANA timezone identifier interpreting the request's business dates, such as `Australia/Brisbane`. A fixed offset is not a timezone and is refused.

GovernedMetricReference.title: GovernedMetricReference
GovernedMetricReference.description: A governed analysis target that is a metric, named by its exact immutable revision identifier. A mutable `latest` alias is not accepted: the revision must be stated.

kind.description: Discriminator for the governed-reference union; constant for this member.

metric_revision_id.description: Exact immutable revision identifier of the approved metric definition. Required on the metric branch and absent on the Data View branch; its presence is what distinguishes the two union members.

GovernedDataViewReference.title: GovernedDataViewReference
GovernedDataViewReference.description: A governed analysis target that is a Data View, named by its exact immutable revision identifier. A mutable `latest` alias is not accepted: the revision must be stated.

kind.description: Discriminator for the governed-reference union; constant for this member.

data_view_revision_id.description: Exact immutable revision identifier of the approved Data View definition. Required on the Data View branch and absent on the metric branch; its presence is what distinguishes the two union members.

AnalysisTarget.title: AnalysisTarget
AnalysisTarget.description: Exactly one governed analysis target: an exact metric revision or an exact Data View revision. The union is discriminated by the required `kind` member unique to each branch.

AnalysisParameter.title: AnalysisParameter
AnalysisParameter.description: One exact typed parameter: a bounded parameter name and its JSON data value. Values are data, never expressions: an executable fragment is not a representable parameter value, and the server interprets parameter meaning only through the governed definition the target names.

name.description: Parameter name as declared by the governed definition.

value.description: The parameter's JSON data value. JSON data only: no expression channel exists in this contract.

AnalysisOutputBounds.title: AnalysisOutputBounds
AnalysisOutputBounds.description: Explicit bounded output. Requested bounds narrow the host and runtime limits; they never override them and never grant execution.

max_rows.description: Maximum returned rows for a bounded Data View read result. Absent means the admitted server profile default.

AnalysisStartInput.title: AnalysisStartInput
AnalysisStartInput.description: Input for `analysis.start`. Workspace-scoped: the workspace is the request envelope's selected workspace; this payload never carries a second, independent workspace identifier. Exactly one temporal scope is stated: an `as_of` business date or an explicit `period` half-open interval, never both and never neither.

request_version.description: The payload schema version this request was authored against, as `major.minor`. Milestone 1 supports `1.0` only.

target.description: The exact governed definition this analysis names.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time business scope: evaluate the governed definition as of this business date in the business timezone. Mutually exclusive with `period`.

period_start.description: Inclusive start of the business-period scope. Required with `period_end` and forbidden with `as_of_date`.

period_end.description: Exclusive end of the business-period scope. Required with `period_start` and forbidden with `as_of_date`.

business_timezone.description: IANA timezone interpreting every business date in this request.

use_class.description: The requested result-use class. Requesting a class does not grant it; the result-use gate evaluates permission separately.

parameters.description: Exact typed parameters, each a name plus JSON data value. Absent means the governed definition's declared defaults apply. Order is not significant; duplicate names are refused.

output_bounds.description: Explicit bounded output. Absent means the admitted server profile default bounds.

purpose_reference.description: Caller-visible reference to the purpose this analysis is requested under. A purpose reference is a claim the service validates; it is never a substitute for identity, authorisation or policy checks.

AnalysisStartResult.title: AnalysisStartResult
AnalysisStartResult.description: Result of `analysis.start`. Reserved in milestone 1: the milestone-1 build never returns a success result, so this type declares no members. It exists so the catalogue's result reference resolves and so a later milestone extends this shape additively rather than inventing a second result type.
